AI Data Centre & AI Infrastructure

AI Data Centre & AI Infrastructure Engineering

AI workloads place different demands on infrastructure than standard enterprise compute: GPU-to-GPU communication is latency-sensitive in a way ordinary application traffic is not, a single stalled node can idle an entire training job, and the network fabric itself becomes a performance bottleneck if it is treated as an afterthought. TechnoKraft provides the engineering, integration, monitoring and managed-service capability to design and operate AI infrastructure with this reality in view, from GPU cluster networking to the NOC and SOC functions that keep it running.

Power → GPU → Fabric → NOC/SOC

Why AI infrastructure requires a different operations model

A standard data centre operations playbook is built around CPU-bound, loosely coupled workloads where a slow server degrades one service. AI training and inference clusters are tightly coupled: GPUs communicate constantly during a distributed training job, coordinated through libraries such as NCCL, and the job runs only as fast as its slowest link. A single degraded InfiniBand port, a misconfigured RDMA queue pair, or unexpected congestion on the leaf-spine fabric does not just slow one workload — it can stall an entire multi-GPU job across dozens of nodes.

This changes what 'monitoring' has to mean. GPU utilisation alone is not a useful health signal if the GPUs are idle while waiting on network communication rather than compute. Effective AI infrastructure operations track network latency and error rates at the fabric level, GPU-to-GPU communication patterns, RDMA and InfiniBand link health, and job-level throughput together, so a bottleneck is diagnosed as a network issue, a driver issue, or a genuine compute limit — rather than assumed to be one when it is another.

The stack

The AI infrastructure stack

A representative AI infrastructure stack, from the physical layer up: power, into the data centre facility, into GPU compute, running on NVIDIA infrastructure where deployed, on a Rocky Linux operating environment, with CUDA and NCCL handling GPU compute and inter-GPU communication, over RDMA, across an InfiniBand or high-speed Ethernet fabric in a leaf-spine network topology, with security and observability layered throughout, feeding into NOC and SOC operations.

This is also why AI infrastructure engagements are staffed differently to a standard data-centre project. A network engineer without GPU-cluster experience can design a technically correct leaf-spine fabric that still under-performs once real training traffic is applied, because the traffic pattern of synchronised gradient exchange across dozens of GPUs does not resemble ordinary application traffic. TechnoKraft's AI infrastructure engagements are staffed by engineers who have worked specifically with GPU networking, not general network engineers applied to a new use case.

  1. L1Power into the data centre facility
  2. L2GPU compute — on NVIDIA infrastructure where deployed
  3. L3Rocky Linux operating environment
  4. L4CUDA and NCCL — GPU compute and inter-GPU communication
  5. L5RDMA across an InfiniBand or high-speed Ethernet fabric
  6. L6Leaf-spine network topology
  7. L7Security and observability layered throughout
  8. L8NOC and SOC operations

What we deliver

Engineering, integration, monitoring and operations

AI Infrastructure Strategy

Architecture planning for GPU compute environments sized to the workload — training, inference, or both — and the growth expected over time.

GPU Cluster Networking

Network fabric design connecting GPU nodes for the throughput and latency distributed training and inference require.

InfiniBand & RDMA

Design, deployment and tuning of InfiniBand fabric and RDMA-based communication for low-latency GPU-to-GPU data transfer.

High-Speed Ethernet

High-speed Ethernet fabric design as an alternative or complement to InfiniBand, depending on workload and existing infrastructure.

Rocky Linux Infrastructure

Operating system deployment and hardening for GPU compute nodes on Rocky Linux environments.

GPU / Network Performance Monitoring

Monitoring GPU utilisation, network latency, InfiniBand and RDMA error rates, and NCCL communication health together, not in isolation.

AI Infrastructure Security

Security controls appropriate to GPU compute environments — network segmentation, access control, and monitoring integrated with the broader Cybersecurity practice.

NOC & SOC

Network and security operations centre functions for AI infrastructure environments, covering both network health and security monitoring.

Infrastructure Automation

Automation of provisioning, configuration and routine operational tasks across GPU compute environments.

Capacity Planning

Planning for GPU, network and storage capacity against current and projected AI workload demand.

Managed AI Infrastructure

Ongoing management of AI compute environments where a client prefers an operating partner to an in-house team.

Engineering, integration and managed services — not a hardware reseller
